cells.tense: You built something that survived a change, and you keep it standing on purpose.
cells.act: give one thing and take one thing, in balance
cells.ask: Take one arrangement you have with someone — who covers what, who gets what — and set both sides onto a single page each of you can reach. Keep it even.
cells.core:
You came through something and what's left is worth keeping. Keeping it isn't passive work — a form holds it up: a way of running the week, a shape the days take. That shape is doing its job. Something changed and what came out of it is still here, still usable, still in your hands.

The next move is to make one arrangement with someone else explicit. Not every obligation — one. Set down what each of you gives and gets, a single page, and keep it somewhere you'll both see it. Exchange runs both ways when it's working. Once both sides are visible, the arrangement stops tilting quietly while you're not looking.
cells.sheetLine: What survived is being held, and it is your hands on it.
cells.verb: Holding what the change produced, in a form that outlasts the change
cells.place: Wherever the pattern for how things run gets set

cells.tense: You're tightening the structure around the result before the result has settled.
cells.act: let yourself be drawn before you choose
cells.ask: Before you lock the next piece of structure into place, give a day to what actually draws you toward it — the pull, no deciding.
cells.core:
You made something and it hasn't finished settling, but the scaffolding keeps going up around it. More rules, more checks, more ways the thing could go wrong — each one laid down before the last has been lived in. The result you're protecting is real. The protection has gotten faster than the thing it protects.

There's pull in this, some of it worth following and some of it just fear of a shape you haven't seen yet. Before you add the next piece, sit with what's drawing you — the feeling, not the plan — and let a day pass before anything gets fixed. What's real will still be there tomorrow. What was only bracing won't be, and you'll know which was which by then.
cells.sheetLine: You're building the cage before the thing inside it wakes.
cells.verb: Holding what the change produced, in a form that outlasts the change

cells.tense: The structure that was holding what you made has gone quiet, and you're still standing at the door.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: Take the piece you decided to keep after the change, and when the next push comes at it, answer once. One answer, then leave it.
cells.core:
You came through a change and something was supposed to be kept. Whatever it was, the structure that held it has gone quiet — the routine around it runs on habit, the decisions that used to feel directed now happen at a remove. You're at the doorway of something you built and you're not quite inside.

Start with direction, not with courage you don't have. Take the piece you decided to keep after the change — not the whole structure — and when something pushes against it, answer once. One push, one answer. That's enough to move. The rest of the structure can come back online after the first piece holds.
cells.sheetLine: You decided to keep something. That decision is still on the books.
cells.verb: Holding what the change produced, in a form that outlasts the change
cells.place: Wherever the pattern for how things run gets set

cells.tense: You're setting the structure everyone is running on, and telling yourself it just happens to be in order.
cells.act: move with the clarity that needs no assertion
cells.ask: When disarray sorts itself out while you're present, pause ten seconds and register that you did that. Then carry on. No announcement.
cells.core:
There's a form taking shape where you go — the way a meeting settles into a rhythm, the way a plan sorts into steps, the way people start knowing what to do. It's running. It's also going unclaimed, and the account of it is that things just got organized around here.

A frame that carries what it holds doesn't need to announce itself, and neither do you. But the making is yours, and it can go recognized. Next time the order appears while you're there, take ten seconds before the next thing — register that you made it — and carry on. Nothing changes except the account, which is the whole of it here.
cells.sheetLine: You're the structure. You call it things settling on their own.
cells.verb: Holding what the change produced, in a form that outlasts the change
cells.place: Wherever the pattern for how things run gets set

attempts.check: The core for the Balanced cell claims the person is actively arranging what they built with other people — the record says nothing about other people; Reciprocity is the medicine, not the record's account of their situation. A reader could reasonably say the balance described is imaginary, since nothing in the kernel says giving and receiving are currently even or that anyone is involved. The ask survives being wrong: sorting a fair arrangement onto paper is useful even if no one else is in the picture, because it makes the arrangement visible. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line about 'the harvest' — pretty, but the record's vocabulary, not the person's life.
